objective: Implement a provider-agnostic, content-addressed project snapshot slice that collects bounded Git evidence, validates immutable candidate projections, records separate acceptance receipts, advances a mutable current pointer only after acceptance, and renders an accepted snapshot read-only.
success_evidence: All three v1alpha1 schemas validate their committed fixtures and invalid fixtures fail for the documented reason.
A local Git repository can produce a content-addressed Evidence Bundle from an explicit source manifest, including dirty state and missing-source diagnostics.
Candidate validation checks schema, digest, timestamps, evidence-bundle identity, evidence-source resolution, and verified-claim evidence without provider-specific behavior.
Acceptance writes a separate immutable receipt and advances current.ref only for an accepted artifact.
The accepted fixture renders as a standalone read-only HTML projection.
The complete automated test suite, Ruff, doctor, CLI smoke flow, and reference render pass on the implementation host.
non_goals: Provider SDKs, live model calls, or a production producer adapter.
A daemon, scheduler, watcher, web server, external database, or network dependency.
Mission Control mutation controls, task writeback, or a polished dashboard redesign.
Broad repository crawling, dependency-tree collection, secret discovery, or arbitrary environment capture.
Changes outside the TORC repository or updates to the Lugos parent submodule pointer.
Inferred completion percentages or provider-dependent validation, storage, acceptance, or rendering.
accepted_threats: SHA-256 supplies local tamper evidence but not writer authentication, confidentiality, or protection from a malicious process with filesystem access.
An explicitly configured non-secret source can still contain sensitive prose; the collector prevents known secret-prone paths but cannot classify all content.
The first renderer is a disposable standalone HTML projection rather than a Mission Control route.
The existing TORC canonical JSON implementation is deterministic for JSON values but is not a complete RFC 8785 implementation.
Windows behavior is contract-tested through portable paths and atomic replace semantics but is not executed on the macOS implementation host.

evidence.target: A committed evidence fixture and candidate fixture pass schema and digest validation, acceptance produces a separate receipt, current.ref advances, and the accepted artifact renders to HTML.
evidence.result: Stable content identity, complete validation checks, separate accepted and rejected receipts, fail-closed current.ref behavior, accepted storage, and read-only HTML passed 14 focused tests before the 20 percent elapsed-effort gate.

platform_matrix.shared_runtime: Python 3.11+ library and CLI with pathlib paths and no service process
platform_matrix.platform_divergence: Only shell invocation syntax differs; storage files, JSON contracts, Git commands, portable current.ref, and os.replace-based writes are shared.
